hero.tagline: Every darkness is a canvas waiting for its stars

today.heading: The listening sky — where light bends into color
today.intro: June tenth. The aurora descends not as spectacle but as conversation — green tendrils reaching across the violet dark, asking the horizon to answer. This is the geometry of wonder: arcs and curtains of charged light, painting the upper atmosphere with the sun's own breath. The night has never been empty. It has only been waiting for eyes willing to see what darkness holds. Below, the hills are still. Above, the sky performs its oldest ceremony — the marriage of solar wind and magnetic field, celebrated in ribbons of emerald and amethyst.

visualAsset.description: Impressionist aurora borealis — vivid green and purple curtains of light sweeping across a starlit sky, with warm amber accents, silhouetted cypress trees, and impressionist brushstroke texture

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: What the night keeps in trust
moon.intro: The Moon does not produce its own radiance — it receives, transforms, and gives back without depletion. Every night it rises as proof that one can shine brilliantly without possessing the source. In the Vedic understanding, the Moon governs not the calculating mind but the feeling heart — the part of us that responds to beauty before language can name it.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Dissolving the outline of the self
philosophy.intro: Arrogance is the wave forgetting it is the sea. For one bright instant the ego believes its own mythology — that it is the author of every crest and the owner of every trough. But the water knows what the wave refuses to: there is no separate self, only currents within currents, patterns within the patternless. To release the fiction of separateness is to discover an ocean where a puddle stood.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: The surrender that is harder than war
gita.intro: Krishna does not ask Arjuna to put down his bow. He asks something far more difficult: to release his grip on why he holds it. The battlefield of Kurukshetra is not a place — it is the condition of being human, caught between duty and desire, action and consequence. The Gita's genius is its refusal to simplify: fight, yes — but fight as the wind fights the sail, without ownership of the destination.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: The sound that precedes creation
shiva.intro: Before the universe had form, it had rhythm. Shiva's damaru — two beats bound together as one drum — is the first oscillation, the original disturbance in silence from which all matter emerges. The Tandava is not performance but physics: every particle vibrates, every wave propagates, every heartbeat echoes that primordial couplet of sound. To still the mind is to hear it still.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: The alchemy of seeing truly
art.intro: A brushstroke is a decision made visible — and every decision carries the ghost of every alternative. The impressionists understood that painting is not the reproduction of light but the revelation of attention. When color is laid down with honesty, the canvas stops being linen and linen-oil-pigment. It becomes a window into the act of perception itself, where the viewer completes what the painter began.
